question.problem: Calculate ${\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s,$ where $C$ is the path along the polar curve $r={e}^{3\theta }$ for $0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
The line integral of unity with respect to arc length over $C$ is equal to the arc length $L$ of $C,$ i.e.,

$$
{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s=L.
$$

In polar coordinates, the arc length element $\text{d}s$ is given by

$$
\text{d}s=\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

So, for a polar curve defined as $r=r(\theta )$ for ${\theta }_{1}\le \theta \le {\theta }_{2},$ we have

$$
L={\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r={e}^{3\theta },$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=3{e}^{3\theta }.
$$

Therefore, we evaluate our line integral as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{({e}^{3\theta })}^{2}+{(3{e}^{3\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{{e}^{6\theta }+9{e}^{6\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\sqrt{10{e}^{6\theta }}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\sqrt{10}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{e}^{3\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}{e}^{3\theta }{|}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{10}}{3}({e}^{3\pi /2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$
